problem: Which of the following gives the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=xy,$ traversed once along the circle $C$ with equation $(x+1)^{2}+{y}^{2}=25?$

activity_context.topic_title: Line Integrals of Scalar Functions Over Circles

examples.knowledge_point: Constructing the Line Integral of a Function Over a Circle
examples.problem: Find, as a definite integral, an expression for the line integral of the function $f(x,y) = x^2-1,$ traversed once along the circle $C$ with equation $x^2 + y^2 = 1.$
examples.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int\limits_C f(x, y) \, \textrm{d}s  = \int\limits_a^b  f(\mathbf r(t)) \, \| \mathbf r'(t) \| \, \textrm{d}t.
$$

 

The curve $C$ is a circle of radius $1$ centered at $O.$ It can be parametrized as 

$$
\mathbf{r}(t) = \big\langle \cos{t}, \: \sin{t} \big\rangle, \qquad 0 \le t \lt 2\pi.
$$

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t)$ and $\| \mathbf{r}'(t) \|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y) = x^2-1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}-1 \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡t-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }({cos}^{2}⁡t-1)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{cos}^{2}⁡t-1\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
